title: The Night Journey and the Hijra
hook: after the night journey and the pledges at 'Aqabah, he slips out of Mecca, hides in a cave, and tells Abu Bakr: do not grieve, Allah is with us

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ta'if. Your line was not them, their children.

After Ta'if, a night. Surah seventeen opens with it, in Pickthall's words: “Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far Distant Place of Worship.” Muslims understand the Far Distant Place as Jerusalem; that night journey is the Isra. Then, they say, came the ascent through the heavens, the Mi'raj, where, a hadith in Bukhari says, the five daily prayers were given. Some early voices held it was a journey of the spirit; others, of body and soul. After the year of sorrow, it is told as an honor and a comfort. At the pilgrimage season, men from Yathrib meet him at night at 'Aqabah and pledge to protect him as they would their own families.
screen: `THE NIGHT JOURNEY.` → `THE FIVE PRAYERS GIVEN.` → `A PLEDGE AT 'AQABAH.`

segments.voice: So the Muslims of Mecca begin leaving for Yathrib, quietly, a few at a time, leaving houses and businesses behind. Quraysh's leaders decide: before he can go, kill him. One young man from each clan, so the blame is shared and his family can't take revenge on anyone. The Qur'an mentions their plotting. That night, the Prophet ﷺ asks 'Ali to sleep in his bed, under his green cloak, and slips out with Abu Bakr. Instead of heading north toward Yathrib, where everyone would look, they go south, up to a cave on Mount Thawr, and hide there three nights. Abu Bakr's daughter Asma' brings food, tearing her waistband in two to tie up the bundles. The trackers come right up to the mouth of the cave. Abu Bakr whispers: if one of them looks down at his feet, he'll see us. The Prophet answers, in Sahih al-Bukhari: what do you think of two, when Allah is the third? Surah At-Tawbah remembers him as “the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us.” People also tell of a spider that spun a web across the cave's mouth, and a dove that nested there, so the trackers thought the cave empty; the Qur'an doesn't mention it, and scholars differ on how reliable the report is. The trackers leave, and the two set out for Yathrib. This leaving is the hijra: the migration, the breaking away. A hadith in Bukhari widens the word: the true emigrant is the one who leaves behind what Allah forbids.
screen: `ONE MAN FROM EACH CLAN.` · `'ALI SLEEPS IN HIS BED.` · `THREE NIGHTS IN THE CAVE OF THAWR.` · `WHAT OF TWO, WHEN ALLAH IS THIRD?` · then, large: `GRIEVE NOT. LO! ALLAH IS WITH US.`

segments.voice: Make a small cave: a closet, a car, or just your hands cupped over your eyes. Let one fear come to the entrance, and whisper, so quietly only you can hear: if you pray, Allah is with us; if you don't, I'm not alone in here.
Hijra. The migration: the Prophet's leaving of Mecca for Yathrib, breaking with the old to begin again.
Your line: Allah is with us. Tomorrow, the last day of the stories. Day ninety-five, done.

screen: `DAY 95 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: CAMP 2 CLOSE: THE CAMEL KNEELS.`

howItsDone: Some communities mark the Isra and Mi'raj on the 27th of Rajab, and the Islamic calendar counts its years from the Hijra.

fork.setup: two men hide in a cave. the trackers are at the entrance. one whispers: if they look down, they'll see us. what does the other say?
options: grieve not; Allah is with us.
fork.reveal: grieve not. lo! Allah is with us (9:40). and in Bukhari: what do you think of two, when Allah is the third?

trapdoor: what you thought: the Prophet moved to Medina.
what it means: hunted by a plot to kill him, he slipped out at night, hid three nights in a cave, and left his home city for a new beginning.

what a scholar hears: 9:40 calls him thani ithnayn, the second of two; the word hijra also means leaving behind what is wrong, and a hadith calls the true emigrant the one who leaves what Allah forbids.
